title: Daemon restart helper: pick up a rebuilt ork without waiting for every role to end
lead: *Options only; this slice waits on the owner decision.* After a landing changes ork itself, the owner has to rebuild the binary by hand and restart the daemon, and a restart refuses while any run works. The slice would shorten that path, but every real fix runs into an owner decision S178 recorded, so no implementation is specified yet.

sections.heading: Why
sections.body:
Friction found in the v1.1 prescan (2026-10-31, friction 3). ork develops itself (adj 166, `engine.self-host`, decided main-binary-restart: the daemon runs a binary built from the base branch, never a worktree; "after a slice that changes internal/engine, internal/daemon or cmd lands, ork offers a daemon restart once no run is active"; `docs/design.md:1757-1790`). The owner's rebuild is a script in the repo root, `run-in-home-dir.sh`: `go build -o ~/bin/ork ./cmd/ork`, `~/bin/ork daemon restart`, `~/bin/ork`.

What blocks a restart: `ork daemon restart` stops the daemon, and `daemon.stop` refuses with `daemon_busy` unless `--force` while a spec check runs, a job is busy, or any run is in a working state (`stopDaemon`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:324-330`; `activeRunsLocked`, `:295-320`). It does not refuse while a run only waits on the owner: `committed`, `stopped`, `paused` and `awaiting-approval` count as at rest (`:312-314`). `--force` cancels the running roles (`docs/design.md:41-48`; `docs/guide.md:391`). The CLI wiring is `daemonCommand` in `internal/cli/lifecycle.go:67-140`.

Why it hurts in v1.1: the plan runs pair waves, two relays at once in two worktrees (owner, 2026-10-31). While either relay works, the daemon is busy, so a landed engine slice cannot be tried in `~/bin/ork` until both relays reach approval or end, and the owner then rebuilds by hand. The "behind main" notice (`BehindNotice`, `internal/daemon/build.go:16`; `docs/dashboard.md`, Self-hosting) tells the owner to run `ork daemon restart`; it does not help with the rebuild.

`ork doctor --upgrade` prints the build commands and runs none of them: `orkHint` builds the list `git -C ORK_CHECKOUT pull --ff-only`, `go -C ORK_CHECKOUT build -o BINARY ./cmd/ork`, `BINARY daemon restart` (`internal/cli/upgrade.go:283-297`).

Slicer check: `slicer find restart` finds ork's S31, S114, S103 and S04 only (S103 clears the stale marker after a restart); `slicer find rebuild` and `slicer find self-update` find nothing. Slicer has no such command.

**The conflict.**

- S178 (done), owner decisions 2026-10-29 (slicer note on S178): "doctor infers each sibling tool's source from the binary and prints the documented commands with ADJ_CHECKOUT and ORK_CHECKOUT placeholders; hints print only when something is behind or missing, and always with --upgrade; doctor never runs them." S178's Why: "The owner runs the commands. ork makes no network call, pulls nothing and builds nothing. This replaces the proposed `ork upgrade` command that would have pulled and built slicer and adj." Its Open 1 rejected a `tools` section in the registry that would record checkout paths (option B), so ork does not know where its own checkout is. These live in a slicer note and in `docs/design.md:1410-1430` (the doctor upgrade hints); `adj check "doctor.upgrade"` and `adj check "tools.upgrade"` return `not found`, so no adj record holds them.
- `docs/design.md:1781` ("ork never restarts the daemon on its own") and `docs/dashboard.md:1727` ("ork never restarts on its own").
- adj 118 (`daemon.legacy-stop`, decided print-pid): ork sends no signal to a daemon that predates `daemon.stop`.
- adj 166: the daemon runs the main-branch binary and the restart is offered, not forced.

A helper that builds, or one that restarts by itself, contradicts one or more of these. A helper that only waits for an idle point and then restarts the current executable does not contradict S178 (it builds nothing), but it is a restart ork performs without the owner pressing a key at that moment, which is what "never restarts on its own" rules out unless the owner has asked for that one restart.

**Options.**

All of these are *proposed*; none is decided.
- A. `ork daemon restart --when-idle`: waits until the daemon is idle (the same test `daemon.stop` uses, or only "no run in a working state"), then stops and starts the current executable. Builds nothing. The owner still builds `~/bin/ork` first. It would hold a CLI process open for as long as the wait lasts (a pair wave can take hours), or return at once and leave a pending restart in the daemon.
- B. `ork upgrade --self` (or `ork daemon rebuild`): builds the ork checkout into the running binary's path with `go build`, then A or a plain restart. Reverses S178 for ork's own binary: ork would run `go`, and would need to know its checkout (a registry field, or the project registered as `ork`).
- C. Make the restart available sooner without any new command: treat a run that waits at `awaiting-approval` as at rest (already true) and have the "behind main" notice name the exact two commands, or print them in the pane. Docs and wording only.
- D. Do nothing; document the script and the pair-wave limitation in `docs/guide.md`.

sections.heading: Files
sections.body:
Waits on the owner decision. The provisional Files per option, for the owner's sizing only:
- A: `internal/cli/lifecycle.go:67-140`, `internal/daemon/runs.go:324-330` (a pending-restart flag if the daemon holds the wait), `internal/daemon/wire.go`, `internal/cli/cli.go:40-77`, `docs/design.md:41-60`, `docs/guide.md:391`, `CHANGELOG.md`. E-class (daemon). UI slice (CLI output).
- B: A plus `internal/cli/upgrade.go`, the registry (a checkout path) or a project lookup, and a supersede of the S178 decision. E-class.
- C: `internal/cli/upgrade.go`, `internal/tui/view.go` (the notice), `docs/dashboard.md`, goldens. N-class.
- D: `docs/guide.md`, `docs/manual-steps.md`, `CHANGELOG.md`. N-class.

sections.heading: Implement
sections.body:
Waits on the owner decision. Do not start. When the owner has decided:
- If B, the owner must first record a decision that changes S178's rule (only the owner supersedes or decides; ork's agents never run `adj reject` or `adj supersede`).
- Then re-spec this slice from the chosen option with Files, named failing tests, Implement steps and Check, test-first, and mark everything the helper adds *proposed* until an adj record decides it.

Owner decisions: 2026-11-07 (interview). Option A: 'ork daemon restart --when-idle'. Option B is not taken.

sections.heading: Check
sections.body: When the Implement section exists: `go test -race -count=1 ./...`; `go vet ./...`; `gofmt -l .`; `slicer check`; `adj lint`; and for a restart helper a [HUMAN CHECK] [AFTER LAND] that the owner restarts a daemon with one run at `awaiting-approval` and one working, with and without the helper.

sections.heading: Git
sections.body: One commit on the slice branch once specified, for example: "Daemon restart helper".
